sessions.name: Open Sesame to the Monolith: Raiding the Legacy Cave with AI Agents
sessions.description:
Every enterprise sits on a "Cave of Wonders".A massive codebase packed with decades of invaluable business logic, hardened edge cases, and customer data. But it's usally locked behind outdated languages, undocumented dependencies, and crushing technical debt. For years, engineers have been forced to act as poor woodcutters, endlessly chopping away at Jira tickets just to keep these systems alive.

That era is over. It is time to speak the new magic words: Agentic AI

In this talk, we will explore how the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents is fundamentally changing software modernization. Using the metaphor of Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, we will break down how to deploy multi-agent systems to safely raid the legacy cave. You will learn how to command a crew of specialized AI agents to autonomously map architecture, generate missing tests, and translate outdated monoliths into modern micro-services.

Abdel will walk you through a real-life example of a team of six engineers modernized a Ruby on Rails application to three programming languages, compared performances, implemented a cloud native architecture and demoed a working prototype to leadership in five days. Using AI Agents to research, code and test along the way.

Key Takeaways:

- Assembling the Crew: How to design a multi-agent architecture where specialized agents handle translation, testing, and documentation. Orchestrated by human engineers.
- Avoiding Cassim’s Trap: Why code is not the only thing that matters in application lifecycle and how the toil of dependencies can break or make a migration project.
- The Morgiana Protocol: How the role of the software engineer is evolving from coder to orchestrator, relying on human-in-the-loop workflows and strict testing to catch hallucinations before they hit production.

speakers.bio:
With over 20 years in the tech industry, Adi is an expert at the intersection of AI, tech startups, and entrepreneurship. Her work is centered on helping startups build successful products and grow, always maintaining a deep focus on the humans behind the users​.

Expertise & Impact:
Driving Startup Success: For 15 years, Adi has served as a Google Developer Expert (GDE) in AI and a Google Accelerator Mentor, where she guides founders in transforming complex AI capabilities into scalable, market-ready products.

Teaching the Next Generation: At Reichman University’s Entrepreneurship School, she teaches Product and AI, dedicated to helping the next generation of entrepreneurs build the skills they need to launch and lead in the tech world.

Humanizing the Tech Space: Through her podcast, "AI & Humans" (Spotify/YouTube), she explores how technology can better serve people, a philosophy she brings to every product she touches.

A Multi-Faceted Life: Adi balances her tech-driven career with a busy home life—she is a mother of four kids, four cats, and a dog, keeping her grounded in the real world.

The Big Picture: Adi combines two decades of high-level experience in AI and product design to help startups scale efficiently while keeping their products human-centered and impactful.

sessions.name: Hardware is Hard, but AI is Smarter: The Robotics "iPhone Moment" is Here
sessions.description:
For years, we’ve said "hardware is hard" to explain why robots haven’t taken over the world yet. But in 2026, the script has flipped. AI is finally giving robotics its "iPhone moment"—turning clunky machines into smart, adaptable agents that can actually understand the physical world.

Whether you are building the next big thing, managing a dev team, or organizing a world-class tech event, you need to know how the "brain" is finally fixing the "body." No dense theory—just the high-octane strategy you need to navigate the new robotic reality.

Why you can't miss this:

The End of Coding Every Move: See how robots are moving from "if-this-then-that" programming to actually reasoning through a task.

The $218B Reality Check: Is the humanoid hype real? We’ll look at the $16,000 robots already entering the workforce.

The "Secret Sauce" of Success: Why the winning robotics startups are actually data companies in disguise.

Spotting the Fakes: A simple cheat sheet to tell the difference between a breakthrough AI play and a fancy remote-controlled toy.

At the end of this talk, you will know:

How to pivot from building static tools to creating autonomous agents.

The 3 "Must-Haves" for any successful robotics project in 2026.

The "Uncanny Valley" Trap: How to design tech that humans actually want to work alongside.

The Future of Labor: Which industries are being "augmented" right now (and who's next).

Ready to see the robots that will soon be making your coffee—and your future strategy? See you there!

speakers.bio: Anuradha is a senior front-end developer, working on making the web more accessible, one website at a time. She is passionate about exploring new technologies and sharing knowledge through tech articles and talks. She has been recognized as GDE, MVP, and WTM Ambassador. As an accessibility advocate, she aims to spread awareness and empower the community toward achieving the common goal of inclusion through technology. When she is not coding, she loves traveling, exploring museums, reading books, and sketching.

sessions.name: Interactions that work for all users
sessions.description:
This talk explores how users interact with websites and how developers can make those interactions accessible to everyone. Using practical examples, such as converting an inaccessible navigation widget or carousel into accessible versions, we’ll explore common accessibility issues and their solutions. The session will include multiple coding demonstrations to illustrate how intentional code changes can significantly impact digital inclusion.

Session takeaway: The audience will understand how users can use the websites in different ways, they will learn different ways to test a scenario, and practical code solutions on how to make the interactions accessible

sessions.name: We are all Fucked: An Android Developer’s Guide to the Post-AI Apocalypse
sessions.description:
AI is dominating Android development, driven by hype over reality. As organizations rush chatbot syntax into production, we are left cleaning up a dumpster fire of unscalable slop. It is time to look past the echo chamber and address our real challenge: protecting codebases from automated pollution.

True engineering relies on architectural rigor and knowing what not to build. This talk is not a chatbot tutorial. Instead, I will share a survival strategy for maintaining codebase integrity when non-technical actors try to treat deliberate software design like an adult colouring book, scribbling shortcuts all over your repo.

You'll walk away with a practical playbook to manage the hype without losing your sanity. Learn how to safeguard repositories, defend quality standards, and strategically isolate your architecture. Ultimately, you will get the tools to distract the tech-bros so you can get back to building actual, resilient software.

speakers.bio:
Brian is a software engineer living in the Lake District, UK. He previously worked on popular desktop, web and mobile applications for Superlist, SoundCloud and Zappos. Furthermore, he's built and contributed to many popular open source libraries, from RxDart to the Flutter Architecture Samples.

In his free time, he's usually found outdoors cycling, hiking, or scuba diving.

sessions.name: GenUI, LLMs driving the user experience, what could go wrong
sessions.description:

This talk will explore the benefits of providing each user with a personalized interface far beyond what has been possible until now. It will also address the challenges this entails, not only in terms of technology, but also product, design, usability, accessibility, legal aspects, and more.

speakers.bio: Cagatay is a Google Developer Expert for Flutter and Dart. After working as a native Android developer in different sizes of companies for a long time, he decided to continue his application development journey with Flutter. He is an active member of the Flutter community and enjoys sharing his knowledge with sample apps, articles, and talks.
speakers.tagLine: Google Developer Expert for Flutter and Dart

sessions.name: GenUI in Production: How GenUI and A2UI Change Mobile Apps
sessions.description:
AI has made it easier to ship apps but not easier to make apps people keep using. The apps that matter will be the ones that fit the person opening them. GenUI is a key enabler in this direction: the design system stays stable while the UI adapts to the user.

We will go from idea to architecture: what GenUI actually is (and is not), how the A2UI protocol makes it backend provide agnostic, and the four ideas that make it possible: surfaces, the catalog, the data model, and the transport.

Then we will dive into learnings from the genui features in production. I will share what production taught me about cost and performance when composing surfaces with GenUI.

I will close with a vision: not static screens for everyone, but screens shaped by what your backend knows about this user, at this moment.

speakers.bio:

sessions.name: AI Printer go brrr
sessions.description:
Every AI demo works fine until it has to touch something real. The model responds, the screenshot looks great, and then you try to wire it up to an actual device and find out how much the screen was covering for you.

So we figured we'd close that gap in front of an audience instead of quietly at home. One prompt, one Genkit flow running on Firebase, Nano Banana doing the generation, and a physical printer at the end of it, live for the whole session, with whatever you throw at it.

The architecture is the part we actually want to talk about. Orchestration ends up mattering more than the model call itself, and we'll show you how a flow gets structured so you can see what each step is doing, how you go about debugging something that breaks three layers down, and what changes when the last thing in your pipeline is a machine that won't negotiate.

One of us builds the flow, the other one gets the hardware to cooperate. We'll find out together whether they meet in the middle.

Expect working code, a lot of paper, and a printer that doesn't stop.

sessions.name: Is Your Repo Agent-Ready? Building a Checklist for the AI Revolution
sessions.description:
Have you heard of AI? Of course you have - it’s likely writing code alongside you every day. But as we move from basic autocompletion to autonomous AI agents, a critical question arises: is your codebase actually built to collaborate with them?

In this talk, I will share my journey of trying to build the ultimate, universal checklist for optimizing repositories for AI agent workflows (especially for enterprise companies). We’ll dive into practical tips, lessons learned, and the unexpected architectural quirks that make or break agentic productivity. Did I succeed in creating the perfect guideline? Join the session and see for yourself!

speakers.bio:
Dr Roushanak Rahmat is an Enterprise AI Architect (Forward Deployed Engineering – GenAI & Agentic AI), Google Developer Expert (AI & Cloud), and recognized as one of the Top 100 Women in Tech (2025). With a PhD in Artificial Intelligence and over 15 years of experience across academia, research, and global enterprise industries, she specialises in designing and delivering large-scale Generative AI, Agentic AI, and advanced Deep Learning systems.

Her work focuses on translating cutting-edge AI research into production-ready enterprise solutions, including LLM-powered systems, RAG architectures, and multi-Agent frameworks across sectors such as healthcare, finance, energy, and retail. She has led enterprise AI transformation initiatives across global organisations and consulting environments, helping clients move from experimentation to scalable, production-grade AI adoption.

sessions.name: Designing Multi‑Agent Systems: Sequential, Parallel, and Beyond with ADK
sessions.description:
Multi‑agent systems are powerful but choosing the wrong interaction pattern can quickly lead to fragile, slow, or expensive AI systems.

In this talk, we explore the core multi‑agent design patterns enabled by ADK, including sequential, parallel, and more advanced coordination models. Rather than focusing on tools alone, we’ll look at how to think architecturally about agent collaboration.

You’ll learn:

When sequential agents are the right choice and when they become a bottleneck

How parallel agents improve speed and coverage (and the trade‑offs they introduce)

Common failure modes in poorly designed agent interactions

Practical criteria for choosing the right pattern based on task, latency, and reliability

By the end of the session, you’ll have a clear mental model for designing multi‑agent systems that are intentional, scalable, and production‑ready.

sessions.name: Gemini Enterprise in Practice: From Secure Access to Real Business Impact
sessions.description:
Gemini Enterprise brings generative AI into the workplace—but adopting it successfully requires more than just enabling a tool.
In this talk, we explore how Gemini Enterprise fits into real organisational environments, focusing on secure access, identity integration, data boundaries, and practical usage patterns. Rather than product demos, we’ll look at how teams actually roll Gemini Enterprise out, what commonly goes wrong, and how to maximise value while staying compliant.
You’ll learn:

How Gemini Enterprise integrates with enterprise identity and access models
Common adoption challenges across security, governance, and change management
Practical usage patterns that drive real productivity—not just experimentation
How to think about Gemini Enterprise as part of a broader AI platform strategy

This session is ideal for developers, tech leads, and architects who want to understand how enterprise GenAI works in practice, not just in theory.

speakers.bio: Communities, tech, strengths. Filip leads GUG.cz, a community that has been educating the Czech Republic in technology for 18 years. At Raynet, he helps evangelize the most popular Czech CRM. In his third and fourth lives, he trains, speaks, and mentors.

sessions.name: Not All APIs Are Created Equal: The Most Useful Skill for 2026
sessions.description:
"We need to talk." A Slack message lands, and your brain has already written the worst-case ending: this is it, I'm getting fired.

That jump from four neutral words to full-blown panic takes milliseconds, and it quietly erodes trust on teams every single day. In this talk we'll show you how to recode that reflex using a method we picked up working alongside the Google community: API (Assume Positive Intent).

We'll unpack why Assume Positive Intent is the cheapest tool you have for raising your team's psychological safety, what it looks like in practice (and what it isn't; this is not naive optimism), and how to start using it before the next ambiguous message spikes your blood pressure.

Along the way, you might accidentally learn something useful about your amygdala, why staying angry is actually a decision and not the default, and (most importantly) how to break the loop.

Fair warning: side effects may include catching yourself smiling at the people around you.

sessions.name: People Aren’t Machines: Collaboration Hacks for Specialists Who’d Rather Talk to Code
sessions.description: You can write flawless code and still watch a project stall because two people read the same message in two different ways. We document our code obsessively and leave the human part to guesswork. Clear collaboration is a skill you can practise, not a personality you are born with. In this talk, I will give you concrete, slightly uncomfortable habits you can use first thing on Monday morning. The same habits that make you easier to work with are the ones that get you picked. No framework you will forget by Friday. Just a few things that make you someone people actually want to work with.

speakers.bio: Karl Weinmeister is the Director of Product Developer Relations at Google Cloud, based in Austin, Texas, USA. Since joining Google in 2018, he has led teams of developer advocates and engineering experts dedicated to empowering builders worldwide through cutting-edge technical content, architectures, and community engagement. His work focuses heavily on Generative AI, agentic systems, and cloud-native architecture. Karl holds an MS in Data Science and an MBA from UT Austin, along with a BS in Computer Science and Economics from Duke University. He was also a key contributor to Proverb, one of the first AI-based crossword puzzle solvers (AAAI Outstanding Paper Award).

sessions.name: The Case of the Missing Velocity (And Other AI Engineering Mysteries, Solved)
sessions.description:
Now that code generation is readily available, software development has evolved into a systems engineering discipline. "Vibe checks" won't cut it when teams need a modern, rigorous SDLC process to keep up. More commits don't necessarily lead to more releases, multi-agent loops can waste tokens, and high test coverage can still hide broken code.

In this keynote, Karl Weinmeister puts on the detective hat to turn AI failure modes into architectural opportunities. Using evidence from developer studies, agent evaluations, and the latest research, Karl shows how to solve each mystery. From strengthening brittle agent loops with high-efficiency agent skills to modern testing and sandboxing strategies, you'll leave with a practical playbook for shipping reliable AI software.

speakers.bio:
Marek Kuruc is a Quantum AI Engineer and researcher at Aricoma, working at the intersection of quantum computing and artificial intelligence.

He is an IBM-certified Qiskit developer and IBM quantum Advocate, focusing on the practical use of both today’s noisy quantum systems and future fault-tolerant quantum computers.

His work spans quantum software development, quantum program optimization, quantum machine learning, and the application of artificial intelligence to quantum computing workflows. He has published research on quantum neural networks executed on current noisy quantum hardware, exploring their capabilities and limitations in real-world conditions.

He works with quantum computing platforms including IBM Quantum, IQM, and IonQ, gaining hands-on experience across different hardware architectures and software ecosystems. He is also involved with NMR-based desktop quantum computers, helping bring accessible, hands-on quantum computing technology to universities and secondary schools.

His broader goal is to bridge the gap between quantum research and practical applications, making emerging quantum technologies useful, accessible, and ready for the next generation of developers and researchers.

sessions.name: Quantum Computing: A New Paradigm for Processing Information
sessions.description:
Quantum computing represents a fundamentally different approach to computation—one that goes beyond simply making existing computers faster. By leveraging quantum-mechanical principles such as superposition, entanglement, and interference, quantum computers introduce new ways of representing, processing, and extracting information from data.
In this talk, we will explore the core ideas behind quantum computing from a software and developer perspective, without requiring a background in quantum physics. We will look at how quantum computation differs from the classical computing model, how quantum algorithms are designed, and why certain classes of problems may benefit from this new computational paradigm.
We will also examine where quantum computing stands today, how quantum processors can work alongside classical CPUs and GPUs in hybrid architectures, and which application areas—from optimization and simulation to machine learning—are actively being explored.
Finally, we will move from theory to practice with demonstrations of quantum circuits and algorithms, explore real-world quantum computing use cases, and take a closer look at the emerging field of Quantum Machine Learning.
The goal is not only to understand how quantum computers work, but to develop an intuition for what it means to build software for an entirely new model of computation

I’ve implemented conversational AI solutions – voice assistants, chatbots, and intelligent interfaces – for organizations including Electrolux, Czech Radio, and enterprise clients across Europe.

And the body matters.



Google Developer Expert – AI/ML

Building the future where AI doesn't just compute. It moves.

sessions.name: Hack a Humanoid: Build Your Own Robot Skills in 100 Minutes
sessions.description:
What would you build if you had access to a real humanoid robot?

Join us for a 100-minute hands-on hackathon with Senti, a Unitree G1 humanoid powered by Sentio OS.

Using our API, you'll be able to control the robot's movements, work with computer vision, access LiDAR data, and create your own robot behaviors.

Form your own team, choose your challenge, and start coding. There are no predefined projects - it's up to you what your robot will do.

Your code. A real humanoid. 100 minutes. Let's see what happens.

speakers.bio: Matěj Kříž is a software engineer and Tech Lead for Trezor Suite, an open-source app spanning web, desktop, and mobile. He has more than a decade of experience building client applications. His work focuses on architecture where security, usability, and data ownership meet. Most recently, his team shipped Suite Sync, a local-first, end-to-end encrypted synchronization layer built with Evolu.

sessions.name: Your App, Their Data: Local-First with Evolu
sessions.description:
Most apps store users’ data on a server and lend it back through an API. Local-first reverses that model: data lives on the user’s device first and remains under their control. The app works without a connection—and can outlive both its servers and the company behind it.

To bring this approach to Trezor Suite across web, desktop, and mobile, we used Evolu: local SQLite, CRDTs, and end-to-end encrypted synchronization through a blind relay.

But giving users ownership of their data does not remove complexity—it moves it. I will share what we learned about key management, schema evolution, deletion, migrations, and storage limits. You will leave with a practical checklist for deciding whether local-first fits your project—and understanding the trade-offs before you commit to it.

speakers.bio:
Mihaela is a Senior Software Architect at Systematic, Romania, and an Oracle ACE Associate for Java. PhD in Artificial Neural Network algorithms, Associate Lecturer at the University of Cybernetics and Informatics in Bucharest, she is passionate about building production-grade systems and bringing real-world experience to the stage.

In her professional career, spanning over 15 years, she has worked in the telecom and defence domains with a focus on Java, Spring Boot, C, C#, Scala and Angular, and a growing interest in AI systems and agentic architectures.

Outside of tech, she loves sports - from running marathons and martial arts to aerobic training - and travels the world whenever she gets the chance.

sessions.name: Building a real-time collaborative editor
sessions.description:
Have you ever wondered what it takes to develop a solution similar to Google Docs and then build on top of it with extra layers of security and functionality?

During the planning phase of a military operation, there are multiple text documents that need to be updated simultaneously by multiple users. At the same time, there is a requirement to provide security in air-gapped deployments.

As such, a solution that follows high standards for security, performance and quality is required.

Within my presentation, I will be describing an embedded solution based on advanced operational transformation algorithms which allows real-time secure collaborative editing, as well as several challenges that we have faced during development and how we managed to overcome each of them.

Peter is also the author of the book "Asynchronous Programming with SwiftUI and Combine: Functional Programming to Build UIs on Apple Platforms" and host of the YouTube show "Firebase After Hours", in which he and his colleagues explore Firebase in a light-hearted and fun setting.

sessions.name: Zero to Shipped: Build a Full-Stack AI App in 90 Minutes
sessions.description:
The way we build software is changing dramatically. Instead of just writing code, we’re now orchestrating  autonomous coding agents that help us build software better and faster than ever before.

But how does it all work? How can you guide your agents to build exactly what you want, instead of producing AI slop?

In this hands-on workshop (bring your laptop!), we will take a deep dive into the modern builder stack. You will learn how to build with a variety of tools from the Google ecosystem.

Come to this session if you want to spend less time configuring and more time creating. Together, we’ll walk through the entire development lifecyclce, from ideation to prototyping, generating a beautiful UI, building powerful AI features, and integrating a secure, scalable backend. 

You will walk away with an app that you can use in your day-to-day life.

sessions.name: The Day I Left My Linux Machine Running: A Love Story with OpenClaw & Hermes
sessions.description:
It was February 5th. I was boarding a flight to South Africa, leaving behind nothing but a beefy Linux machine named pupurabbux and a restless curiosity about automation. Little did I know that by February 7th, my entire world would shift on its axis.
Join me for a whirlwind journey from standard engineering to AI-fueled enlightenment as I recount how Hermes and OpenClaw didn't just optimize my workflows—they redefined my reality.
This is a story of serendipity, digital alchemy, and the day I realized that my server at home was doing more than just running scripts—it was running my life.

sessions.name: Can an LLM understand your car? Real telemetry and predictive insights
sessions.description:
Modern cars produce far more data than what appears on the dashboard: sensor readings, diagnostic codes, pressure changes, temperature values, service intervals, and component health trends.

In this talk, we’ll explore how to turn telemetry collected from different real Porsche sports cars into clear, useful insights using a structured LLM-based analysis pipeline. We’ll detect measurable signals such as declining health, warning states, critical sensors, performance patterns, and upcoming maintenance needs. Then we’ll use an LLM as an explanation layer to summarize driving behavior, anomalies, and maintenance signals.

The goal is not to let the LLM control the car or replace expert inspection, but to make complex telemetry easier to understand, explain, and act on.

sessions.name: Not All APIs Are Created Equal: The Most Useful Skill for 2026
sessions.description:
"We need to talk." A Slack message lands, and your brain has already written the worst-case ending: this is it, I'm getting fired.

That jump from four neutral words to full-blown panic takes milliseconds, and it quietly erodes trust on teams every single day. In this talk we'll show you how to recode that reflex using a method we picked up working alongside the Google community: API (Assume Positive Intent).

We'll unpack why Assume Positive Intent is the cheapest tool you have for raising your team's psychological safety, what it looks like in practice (and what it isn't; this is not naive optimism), and how to start using it before the next ambiguous message spikes your blood pressure.

Along the way, you might accidentally learn something useful about your amygdala, why staying angry is actually a decision and not the default, and (most importantly) how to break the loop.

Fair warning: side effects may include catching yourself smiling at the people around you.

sessions.title: Gemini Enterprise in Practice: From Secure Access to Real Business Impact
sessions.description:
Gemini Enterprise brings generative AI into the workplace—but adopting it successfully requires more than just enabling a tool.
In this talk, we explore how Gemini Enterprise fits into real organisational environments, focusing on secure access, identity integration, data boundaries, and practical usage patterns. Rather than product demos, we’ll look at how teams actually roll Gemini Enterprise out, what commonly goes wrong, and how to maximise value while staying compliant.
You’ll learn:

How Gemini Enterprise integrates with enterprise identity and access models
Common adoption challenges across security, governance, and change management
Practical usage patterns that drive real productivity—not just experimentation
How to think about Gemini Enterprise as part of a broader AI platform strategy

This session is ideal for developers, tech leads, and architects who want to understand how enterprise GenAI works in practice, not just in theory.

The Case of the Missing Velocity (And Other AI Engineering Mysteries, Solved)
sessions.description:
Now that code generation is readily available, software development has evolved into a systems engineering discipline. "Vibe checks" won't cut it when teams need a modern, rigorous SDLC process to keep up. More commits don't necessarily lead to more releases, multi-agent loops can waste tokens, and high test coverage can still hide broken code.

In this keynote, Karl Weinmeister puts on the detective hat to turn AI failure modes into architectural opportunities. Using evidence from developer studies, agent evaluations, and the latest research, Karl shows how to solve each mystery. From strengthening brittle agent loops with high-efficiency agent skills to modern testing and sandboxing strategies, you'll leave with a practical playbook for shipping reliable AI software.

sessions.title: Open Sesame to the Monolith: Raiding the Legacy Cave with AI Agents
sessions.description:
Every enterprise sits on a "Cave of Wonders".A massive codebase packed with decades of invaluable business logic, hardened edge cases, and customer data. But it's usally locked behind outdated languages, undocumented dependencies, and crushing technical debt. For years, engineers have been forced to act as poor woodcutters, endlessly chopping away at Jira tickets just to keep these systems alive.

That era is over. It is time to speak the new magic words: Agentic AI

In this talk, we will explore how the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents is fundamentally changing software modernization. Using the metaphor of Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, we will break down how to deploy multi-agent systems to safely raid the legacy cave. You will learn how to command a crew of specialized AI agents to autonomously map architecture, generate missing tests, and translate outdated monoliths into modern micro-services.

Abdel will walk you through a real-life example of a team of six engineers modernized a Ruby on Rails application to three programming languages, compared performances, implemented a cloud native architecture and demoed a working prototype to leadership in five days. Using AI Agents to research, code and test along the way.

Key Takeaways:

- Assembling the Crew: How to design a multi-agent architecture where specialized agents handle translation, testing, and documentation. Orchestrated by human engineers.
- Avoiding Cassim’s Trap: Why code is not the only thing that matters in application lifecycle and how the toil of dependencies can break or make a migration project.
- The Morgiana Protocol: How the role of the software engineer is evolving from coder to orchestrator, relying on human-in-the-loop workflows and strict testing to catch hallucinations before they hit production.

sessions.title: Zero to Shipped: Build a Full-Stack AI App in 90 Minutes
sessions.description:
The way we build software is changing dramatically. Instead of just writing code, we’re now orchestrating  autonomous coding agents that help us build software better and faster than ever before.

But how does it all work? How can you guide your agents to build exactly what you want, instead of producing AI slop?

In this hands-on workshop (bring your laptop!), we will take a deep dive into the modern builder stack. You will learn how to build with a variety of tools from the Google ecosystem.

Come to this session if you want to spend less time configuring and more time creating. Together, we’ll walk through the entire development lifecyclce, from ideation to prototyping, generating a beautiful UI, building powerful AI features, and integrating a secure, scalable backend. 

You will walk away with an app that you can use in your day-to-day life.

sessions.title: Break
GenUI in Production: How GenUI and A2UI Change Mobile Apps
sessions.description:
AI has made it easier to ship apps but not easier to make apps people keep using. The apps that matter will be the ones that fit the person opening them. GenUI is a key enabler in this direction: the design system stays stable while the UI adapts to the user.

We will go from idea to architecture: what GenUI actually is (and is not), how the A2UI protocol makes it backend provide agnostic, and the four ideas that make it possible: surfaces, the catalog, the data model, and the transport.

Then we will dive into learnings from the genui features in production. I will share what production taught me about cost and performance when composing surfaces with GenUI.

I will close with a vision: not static screens for everyone, but screens shaped by what your backend knows about this user, at this moment.

sessions.title: Quantum Computing: A New Paradigm for Processing Information
sessions.description:
Quantum computing represents a fundamentally different approach to computation—one that goes beyond simply making existing computers faster. By leveraging quantum-mechanical principles such as superposition, entanglement, and interference, quantum computers introduce new ways of representing, processing, and extracting information from data.
In this talk, we will explore the core ideas behind quantum computing from a software and developer perspective, without requiring a background in quantum physics. We will look at how quantum computation differs from the classical computing model, how quantum algorithms are designed, and why certain classes of problems may benefit from this new computational paradigm.
We will also examine where quantum computing stands today, how quantum processors can work alongside classical CPUs and GPUs in hybrid architectures, and which application areas—from optimization and simulation to machine learning—are actively being explored.
Finally, we will move from theory to practice with demonstrations of quantum circuits and algorithms, explore real-world quantum computing use cases, and take a closer look at the emerging field of Quantum Machine Learning.
The goal is not only to understand how quantum computers work, but to develop an intuition for what it means to build software for an entirely new model of computation

sessions.title: Lunch
AI Printer go brrr
sessions.description:
Every AI demo works fine until it has to touch something real. The model responds, the screenshot looks great, and then you try to wire it up to an actual device and find out how much the screen was covering for you.

So we figured we'd close that gap in front of an audience instead of quietly at home. One prompt, one Genkit flow running on Firebase, Nano Banana doing the generation, and a physical printer at the end of it, live for the whole session, with whatever you throw at it.

The architecture is the part we actually want to talk about. Orchestration ends up mattering more than the model call itself, and we'll show you how a flow gets structured so you can see what each step is doing, how you go about debugging something that breaks three layers down, and what changes when the last thing in your pipeline is a machine that won't negotiate.

One of us builds the flow, the other one gets the hardware to cooperate. We'll find out together whether they meet in the middle.

Expect working code, a lot of paper, and a printer that doesn't stop.

sessions.title: Your App, Their Data: Local-First with Evolu
sessions.description:
Most apps store users’ data on a server and lend it back through an API. Local-first reverses that model: data lives on the user’s device first and remains under their control. The app works without a connection—and can outlive both its servers and the company behind it.

To bring this approach to Trezor Suite across web, desktop, and mobile, we used Evolu: local SQLite, CRDTs, and end-to-end encrypted synchronization through a blind relay.

But giving users ownership of their data does not remove complexity—it moves it. I will share what we learned about key management, schema evolution, deletion, migrations, and storage limits. You will leave with a practical checklist for deciding whether local-first fits your project—and understanding the trade-offs before you commit to it.

sessions.title: Hardware is Hard, but AI is Smarter: The Robotics "iPhone Moment" is Here
sessions.description:
For years, we’ve said "hardware is hard" to explain why robots haven’t taken over the world yet. But in 2026, the script has flipped. AI is finally giving robotics its "iPhone moment"—turning clunky machines into smart, adaptable agents that can actually understand the physical world.

Whether you are building the next big thing, managing a dev team, or organizing a world-class tech event, you need to know how the "brain" is finally fixing the "body." No dense theory—just the high-octane strategy you need to navigate the new robotic reality.

Why you can't miss this:

The End of Coding Every Move: See how robots are moving from "if-this-then-that" programming to actually reasoning through a task.

The $218B Reality Check: Is the humanoid hype real? We’ll look at the $16,000 robots already entering the workforce.

The "Secret Sauce" of Success: Why the winning robotics startups are actually data companies in disguise.

Spotting the Fakes: A simple cheat sheet to tell the difference between a breakthrough AI play and a fancy remote-controlled toy.

At the end of this talk, you will know:

How to pivot from building static tools to creating autonomous agents.

The 3 "Must-Haves" for any successful robotics project in 2026.

The "Uncanny Valley" Trap: How to design tech that humans actually want to work alongside.

The Future of Labor: Which industries are being "augmented" right now (and who's next).

Ready to see the robots that will soon be making your coffee—and your future strategy? See you there!

sessions.title: Big Break
We are all Fucked: An Android Developer’s Guide to the Post-AI Apocalypse
sessions.description:
AI is dominating Android development, driven by hype over reality. As organizations rush chatbot syntax into production, we are left cleaning up a dumpster fire of unscalable slop. It is time to look past the echo chamber and address our real challenge: protecting codebases from automated pollution.

True engineering relies on architectural rigor and knowing what not to build. This talk is not a chatbot tutorial. Instead, I will share a survival strategy for maintaining codebase integrity when non-technical actors try to treat deliberate software design like an adult colouring book, scribbling shortcuts all over your repo.

You'll walk away with a practical playbook to manage the hype without losing your sanity. Learn how to safeguard repositories, defend quality standards, and strategically isolate your architecture. Ultimately, you will get the tools to distract the tech-bros so you can get back to building actual, resilient software.

sessions.title: Designing Multi‑Agent Systems: Sequential, Parallel, and Beyond with ADK
sessions.description:
Multi‑agent systems are powerful but choosing the wrong interaction pattern can quickly lead to fragile, slow, or expensive AI systems.

In this talk, we explore the core multi‑agent design patterns enabled by ADK, including sequential, parallel, and more advanced coordination models. Rather than focusing on tools alone, we’ll look at how to think architecturally about agent collaboration.

You’ll learn:

When sequential agents are the right choice and when they become a bottleneck

How parallel agents improve speed and coverage (and the trade‑offs they introduce)

Common failure modes in poorly designed agent interactions

Practical criteria for choosing the right pattern based on task, latency, and reliability

By the end of the session, you’ll have a clear mental model for designing multi‑agent systems that are intentional, scalable, and production‑ready.

sessions.title: Is Your Repo Agent-Ready? Building a Checklist for the AI Revolution
sessions.description:
Have you heard of AI? Of course you have - it’s likely writing code alongside you every day. But as we move from basic autocompletion to autonomous AI agents, a critical question arises: is your codebase actually built to collaborate with them?

In this talk, I will share my journey of trying to build the ultimate, universal checklist for optimizing repositories for AI agent workflows (especially for enterprise companies). We’ll dive into practical tips, lessons learned, and the unexpected architectural quirks that make or break agentic productivity. Did I succeed in creating the perfect guideline? Join the session and see for yourself!

sessions.title: Bright future for software development (and why my developers disagree)
sessions.description:
This is not a talk about AI. It is a talk about the people who have to live with it, and about what the new way of work actually costs them.

I spend my days designing future - a system where AI agents write most of our software. This is a fundamental change to digital product building and many people are afraid of what's next.

I will show you what impacts my (and probably your) people most and what we are doing about it at Applifting.

I still think the future is bright. It will just take more work, and more sacrifices, than anyone puts on a slide.

sessions.title: Break
Building a real-time collaborative editor
sessions.description:
Have you ever wondered what it takes to develop a solution similar to Google Docs and then build on top of it with extra layers of security and functionality?

During the planning phase of a military operation, there are multiple text documents that need to be updated simultaneously by multiple users. At the same time, there is a requirement to provide security in air-gapped deployments.

As such, a solution that follows high standards for security, performance and quality is required.

Within my presentation, I will be describing an embedded solution based on advanced operational transformation algorithms which allows real-time secure collaborative editing, as well as several challenges that we have faced during development and how we managed to overcome each of them.

sessions.title: GenUI, LLMs driving the user experience, what could go wrong
sessions.description:
Current LLMs and models are powerful enough to generate real-time, context-based interfaces for each user.

This talk will explore the benefits of providing each user with a personalized interface far beyond what has been possible until now. It will also address the challenges this entails, not only in terms of technology, but also product, design, usability, accessibility, legal aspects, and more.

sessions.description: You can write flawless code and still watch a project stall because two people read the same message in two different ways. We document our code obsessively and leave the human part to guesswork. Clear collaboration is a skill you can practise, not a personality you are born with.
